subject: C29
required_fixes: R1 — crates/desktop-core/src/store.rs:294–325,578 and authority.rs:1895–1903: a saved draft credential makes the production document fail its next load. persisted() includes draft-owned Keychain credentials, but is_consistent() accepts credential owners only from committed tenants. FileStore::load therefore returns Corrupt before data_from can discard the draft and clean its records; in add mode existing tenants also become unavailable. The restart test uses ScriptedStore/MemoryStore, which skips this validation. Acceptance: production FileStore round-trips keyed first-run and add drafts, validates their ownership, and relaunch discards only the draft and cleans its credentials while preserving existing data.

R2 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:5397–5400,5475–5480; authority/setup_domain.rs:209–236; authority/management_domain.rs:82–110; management.rs:1536–1576: draft credential replacement and TSG/destination edits preserve the setup context without retiring its management binding. That binding is cached by context, and its OnceCell retains the earlier SDK clients, credentials, token cache and TSG. A new verification can therefore pass using the old client after replacement with an invalid one, keep failing after a correction, or read the earlier TSG under the edited profile. Acceptance: production-interface tests initialize a binding, replace/remove/re-add credentials and change TSG, then prove fresh authentication and targets; old operations/results and cached authority must retire, including on discard.

R3 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/gateway_domain.rs:159–211,216–247 and authority/management_domain.rs:294–336: the active tenant and setup draft now coexist, but Gateway still has one global listing/selection. A draft's complete workspace listing can clear the active tenant's selection and cancel its workspace operations; choosing a draft workspace replaces that global selection. gateway_listed also restores from data.active instead of the listing's tenant. Discard does not restore the original state. Acceptance: with tenant A's workspace selected and work pending, list/select/verify tenant B's draft and cancel it; A's workspace reference, metadata and work remain unchanged, and late B replies cannot affect A.

R4 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:1845–1851,3527–3540: tenant() now includes the setup draft, so SelectTenant accepts the draft ID exposed in setup.tenant.id. It changes active selection before completion and saves an active_tenant absent from the committed tenant list; discarding the draft then leaves a dangling active identity. Acceptance: selecting a draft ID through the production authority/IPC is refused without changing selection, context or persisted state; only successful setup completion promotes and selects it.

R5 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority.rs:1735–1741; authority/setup_domain.rs:184–185; apps/desktop/src/app.tsx:173–203: successful first-run import is still a dead end. Leaving Welcome sets InProgress; C23 imports tenants without changing that state, while shown_onboarding only handles existing tenants when state is Needed. Back to setup renders a firstRun wizard whose beginTenantSetup is now refused because tenants exist. My production-App probe with this post-import state remained on Your tenant and displayed InvalidInput. Acceptance: approve a tenant import during first run and return to usable fresh credential setup for the imported identity, without requiring a duplicate tenant or abandoning onboarding; cover restart too.

R6 — apps/desktop/src/v2/v2-shell.tsx:60–64: Cancel hides the sheet before discard is confirmed and ignores every dispatch outcome. My refused-discard probe closed the dialog with no error or retry while the draft remained. Unknown delivery and cancellation while draft creation is pending are likewise unreconciled. Acceptance: Cancel/Escape/scrim exits visibly handle refused, failed and unknown discards, reconcile observed draft state, and do not claim cancellation or lose access to cleanup while a draft/credential remains.

R7 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:79–87,110–134,219–221,451: local profile edits bypass validation and invalidation until Save changes is explicitly pressed. After a verified setup, my probe cleared TSG to an aria-invalid value; Continue and the visited Done rail remained enabled, and Open sent completeTenantSetup over the earlier profile. Acceptance: dirty or invalid displayed details cannot silently complete using older values; save/validate them or require an explicit discard, invalidate downstream eligibility, and verify the committed current inputs.

R8 — apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:71,224–227,249,255 and authority/setup_domain.rs:631–632: explicit starter-pack selection is never reconciled when products change. Removing Gateway after selecting its pack leaves a hidden gateway entry in selectedPacks; my probe sent packs:[gateway] with only Runtime selected, which Rust correctly refuses. Acceptance: product removal removes or explicitly resolves incompatible pack choices, the summary matches visible selections, and completion succeeds with only currently selected product packs.

R9 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/setup_domain.rs:381–390,465–480 and apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:239–245,493–506: required verification coverage remains reduced. Gateway only lists workspaces and passes when any exists; it never reads the selected workspace's admitted GatewayRead::Prerequisites required by screens/wizard.md. AIS/AES also disappear from Verify instead of being listed as Not available. Acceptance: verify the selected Gateway workspace's actual prerequisites, expose missing/partial coverage honestly, invalidate on relevant workspace changes, and render unavailable products without dispatching checks or inventing results.

R10 — crates/desktop-core/src/authority/setup_domain.rs:579–581,623–624 and apps/desktop/src/v2/wizard/wizard.tsx:511–517: a failed optional service check cannot take the specified Continue with warnings path. All failures block completion, and only Warning states become Inbox warnings. The board test explicitly asserts this reduced behavior. Acceptance: with required credentials present, an operator can explicitly continue after an optional check fails, preserving its product/reason as a warning at completion without converting failure to Pass; stale/context/required-credential guards remain enforced.

R11 — apps/desktop/src-tauri/tests/ipc_admission.rs:554–650 and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:220–229: the new mock-host test dispatches verifyTenantSetup with a configured synthetic management credential, but fixture_core() retains CoreConfig::default() production management URLs and the real HTTP transport. The test can therefore attempt product OAuth/reads during ordinary host checks, and accepts any settled verification without proving fixture isolation. Acceptance: use explicitly controlled synthetic endpoints/transport, fail on unintended network access, and assert the expected synthetic verification result; routine tests must never contact product services.
blockers: B1 — docs/planning/evidence/C29/live/blocked.json confirms no Vulture verification ran because the management read lacks approved designation. C29.md makes this live receipt mandatory and missing access blocking. Obtain the owner-designated read-only scope and retain a redacted receipt from the actual reviewed verification workflow; synthetic acceptance cannot satisfy this row.
evidence_gaps: E1 — tools/native-acceptance/acceptance_c29.py:164–175 labels the initial capture light-100 without selecting Light. For all seven wizard steps, the retained light-100 image is byte-for-byte identical to dark-100; inspected examples visibly use the dark theme. N06 passes by counting filenames, so the mandatory light/dark 100%/200% matrix is not established. Explicitly select and verify each theme/zoom, regenerate the actual matrix and native record on the corrected bundle, and retain the matching hashes.

E2 — The passing tests do not establish the critical production transitions above. In particular, the relaunch test bypasses FileStore consistency, native credential recovery restores the synthetic endpoint rather than replacing a rejected client, and add-mode acceptance never exercises an existing tenant's Gateway selection alongside a draft. Add causal production-interface regressions for the findings, including successful import, cancellation failures and pack/product edits, then rerun affected source-bound checks and native acceptance.
